//: Type-checking config for the browser-side files (static/**/*.js). They are
plain ES modules, not TypeScript, so `deno check` ignores them entirely
unless `checkJs` is on — without it the check passes on an undeclared
identifier, which is exactly the class of bug it exists to catch.
This lives apart from deno.json because the flags have to differ. Browser
code here is untyped by design — parameters carry no annotations — so
`noImplicitAny` is off. `strictNullChecks` is deliberately kept ON: without
it TypeScript cannot narrow a discriminated union, so every `if (!r.ok)`
guard in the codebase would report a false error on `r.error`.
`lib` needs `dom`, which the Deno default omits.
